title: God Comes Down to Our Level

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So the Lord said to him, "Bring me a heifer, a goat and a ram, each three years old, along with a dove and a young pigeon." Abram brought all these to him, cut them in two and arranged the halves opposite each other; the birds, however, he did not cut in half. - Gen 15:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God answers Abram's "how can I know?" in a way that must have made perfect sense to him - and looks strange to us. He asks for animals to be cut in half and laid opposite each other, forming a path between the pieces. This was the ancient way of making a binding covenant. Two parties would walk between the severed animals, saying in effect: may this happen to me if I break my word.

Notice what God is doing. He is speaking Abram's language. He could have simply said, "Trust me." Instead, He stoops to use a ritual Abram already understood, meeting him in his own culture and time.

This is how God always works. He comes down to where we are. He speaks in ways we can grasp - through stories, through pictures, through bread and wine we can hold in our hands. God is not distant and abstract; He condescends to our capacity.

The greatest condescension of all was the incarnation, when "the Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us" (John 1:14). God did not shout instructions from heaven; He came and stood among us. Whatever your questions, God is willing to meet you where you are. He is not too proud to come down to your level.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you picture God as distant, or as One who comes down to meet you?
- How has God met you in ways you could actually understand?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You come down to my level and speak in ways I can grasp. Thank You supremely for Jesus, who came and dwelt among us. Meet me where I am today.
Amen.
